data.name: Og
data.long_meaning: In biblical texts, Og is described as a giant or a strong leader. The name may have derived from the Hebrew word 'og' meaning 'giant' or 'monster'. In Numbers 21:33-35, Og is mentioned as the last king of Bashan, whose bed was a bedstead of iron.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength and power, both in physical and spiritual senses.

in_hebrew.name: עוֹג
in_hebrew.meaning: שם מלך עמון שהיה גדול ומפורסם
in_hebrew.long_meaning: במקרא, עוֹג (עברית: עוֹג) היה נסיך עמון, חברו של רב־עמל, ושליט יששכר. עוֹג נזכר בספר במדבר (21:13–24) כמלך עמון. שם עוֹג נזכר גם במקור עברי לאדם גדול, או לדבר גדול.

in_greek.name: Ωγ
in_greek.meaning: βασιλιάς των Αμωνούς, μεγάλος και φαμαρκός
in_greek.long_meaning: Στην Βίβλο, Ωγ (Ελληνικά: Ωγ) ήταν βασιλιάς των Αμωνούς. Ένας από τους μεγαλύτερους βασιλείς στην lịchη Βίβλο. Ο Ωγ είναι ένα από τα πιο γνωστά ονόματα στους Βιβλικούς αιώνες.

in_latin.name: Og
in_latin.long_meaning: In Biblia, Og (Latin: Og) fuit rex Moaborum, unus magnorum regum in antiqua historia. Nomen Og a fontibus Hebraeo-Graecis originem ducit, et significat regem magni et famosi.

in_english.name: Og
in_english.meaning: king of the Ammonites, great and famous
in_english.long_meaning: In the Bible, Og (English: Og) was the king of the Ammonites, one of the greatest kings in ancient history. The name Og originates from the Hebrew and Greek roots, and it means a great and famous king.

biblical_reference.note: Og was a king of the Ammonites who lived in the time of Moses.
